newsitem.title: USA: Compaq's net income slips due to Microcom charge.
newsitem.headline: Compaq's net income slips due to Microcom charge.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. said Thursday its second-quarter profits fell by 20 percent as it took a $208 million charge related to its acquisition of Microcom Inc.

The company, the world's largest supplier of personal computers, said its net income for the three months ended June 30 declined to $214 million, or 75 cents a share, from $267 million, or 97 cents a share.
Revenues, however, shot up by 25 percent to $5.01 billion from $4.0 billion.
Compaq said the $208 million charge it took to write off purchased in-process technology in the Microcom deal knocked 73 cents off its earnings per share.
Without the charge, Compaq said, its second-quarter net income would have been $422 million, or $1.48 a share.
Wall Street had been expecting the company to post income of $1.39 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Compaq acquired Microcom, a manufacturer of modems and other remote access technologies in Norwood, Mass., for $280 million in April.
Houston-based Compaq also said that it ended the second quarter with a cash balance of $5.1 billion, including cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments.
Compaq said that its cash increased 165 percent as a result of operational improvements and asset management, such as its increased inventory turns, and fewer sales days outstanding.
For the first six months of the year, Compaq said, net income climbed by 20 percent to $601 million, or $2.12 cents a share, from $501 million, or $1.81 cents a share.
Revenues expanded to $9.8 billion from $8.2 billion.
